---
title: "Global spatially variable feature baselines in R: SPARK-X and nnSVG"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

These methods test whether a feature varies in space **without** conditioning on cell type. We use them as (i) baselines, and (ii) **within-cell-type** tests, by running them on the cells of a single type. That is the simplest ctSVP strategy for single-cell imaging data.

```{r install}
devtools::install_github("xzhoulab/SPARK")
BiocManager::install(c("nnSVG", "SpatialExperiment", "scuttle", "Statial"))
```

## Data: Keren 2018 MIBI (`kerenSCE`)

```{r data}
library(Statial); library(SingleCellExperiment)
data("kerenSCE")
img    <- kerenSCE[, kerenSCE$imageID == unique(kerenSCE$imageID)[1]]
expr   <- assay(img, "intensities")
coords <- as.matrix(colData(img)[, c("x", "y")]); rownames(coords) <- colnames(img)
```

## SPARK-X: non-parametric kernel covariance test, linear in n

Top performer in the 2025 Genome Biology benchmark of 14 SVG methods. It is also the best-calibrated.

```{r sparkx}
library(SPARK)
# Global test
sx <- sparkx(count_in = expr, locus_in = coords, numCores = 4, option = "mixture")
head(sx$res_mtest[order(sx$res_mtest$adjustedPval), ])   # combinedPval, adjustedPval

# Within-cell-type test = a simple ctSVP detector
ctsv_sparkx <- lapply(split(colnames(img), img$cellType), function(cells) {
  if (length(cells) < 50) return(NULL)                    # too few cells for a stable test
  r <- sparkx(expr[, cells], coords[cells, ], numCores = 4, verbose = FALSE)$res_mtest
  data.frame(feature = rownames(r), p_value = r$combinedPval)
})
```

## nnSVG: nearest-neighbour Gaussian process with feature-specific length scale

```{r nnsvg}
library(nnSVG); library(SpatialExperiment)
spe <- SpatialExperiment(assays = list(logcounts = asinh(expr / 5)),   # arcsinh-transformed intensities
                         spatialCoords = coords)
spe <- nnSVG(spe, assay_name = "logcounts", n_threads = 4)
head(as.data.frame(rowData(spe))[order(rowData(spe)$rank), c("LR_stat", "prop_sv", "pval", "padj", "rank")])
# prop_sv = spatial variance / total variance: an interpretable effect size
```
